#!/bin/sh

cd "${WINEPREFIX:-$HOME/.wine}"
cd "drive_c/users/USER/Local Settings/Application Data/Warframe/Downloaded/Public/Tools"

# pass script's arguments to "Launcher.exe"
wine ./Launcher.exe "$@" &

sleep 3m

if [ -e "Launcher.exe.cpy" ]
then

 # wait while it's written to (?)
 while [ `lsof "Launcher.exe.cpy"` ]
 do
 sleep 1
 done

 # swap files
 oldtime=$(stat -c '%y' "Launcher.exe")
 mv "Launcher.exe" "Launcher.exe.old.$oldtime"
 mv "Launcher.exe.cpy" "Launcher.exe"
fi

# optional: wait for bg process
wait

You could move the user name into a variable for easier editing: user="username" ; cd "drive/c_users/$user/..."

Also, instead of the extra WINEPREFIX= expression in front of wine ./Launcher.exe, you could set WINEPREFIX before the first cd. Although ${WINEPREFIX: is intended so you can change the wine prefix path exterior to the script, so if you want that to be a fixed value instead, you could simplify the part before sleep to:

# EDIT THIS: change to the prefix/bottle you installed Warframe to.
WINEPREFIX="$HOME/.wine"

 # EDIT THIS: change "username" to your user name if it's different from the system user.
wine_username="$USER"

# NO NEED TO EDIT PAST THIS POINT

cd "$WINEPREFIX"
cd "drive_c/users/$wine_username/Local Settings/Application Data/Warframe/Downloaded/Public/Tools"

WINEPREFIX="$WINEPREFIX" wine ./Launcher.exe

The separate cd to $WINEPREFIX makes the paths more flexible (acts the same whether users leave a trailing slash on the path). "WINEPREFIX" is uppercase to match what the wine executable reads. "wine_username" is lowercase to avoid conflicting with any other wine-related environment variables, but to distinguish it as specific to what we're using it for. Likely you could dispense with wine_username and use $USER instead, but I don't know wine enough to tell.

edit: Forgot that the WINEPREFIX value wasn't exported, still need that before calling wine.
